docs.text: API Specification (OpenAPI) ¶ The full OpenAPI YAML is included in the repo: Openapi_Spec_InvestorInboxProcessAPI.yaml OpenAPI 3.0 Specification (YAML) ¶ openapi : 3.0.3 info : title : InvestorInboxProcessAPI version : 1.0.0 description : > Internal process-layer API responsible for orchestration, validation, transformation and unread-count computation for the investor message inbox. servers : - url : https://internal.api.local/inbox-process description : Internal-only endpoint (not exposed to internet) paths : /unread-messages : post : summary : Fetch unread messages for a user (system + bulk) description : > Aggregates unread messages (system and bulk) for a given user, applies validation and transformation, and returns a unified DTO including totalUnread. This endpoint is intended to be called by InvestorInboxChannelAPI. requestBody : required : true content : application/json : schema : type : object required : - userId properties : userId : type : string description : "Unique identifier of the investor user" includeRead : type : boolean description : "If true, include read messages as well" default : false responses : "200" : description : Unread messages aggregated for the user content : application/json : schema : $ref : "#/components/schemas/UnreadMessagesResult" "400" : description : Invalid request (e.g. missing userId) "401" : description : Caller is not authorised to invoke this process API "500" : description : Downstream failure (system API / bulk API / unexpected error) /message-detail : post : summary : Fetch detailed content for a single message description : > Retrieves and validates the full details of a specific message, ensuring it belongs to the requester and mapping raw fields to MessageDetailDTO. requestBody : required : true content : application/json : schema : type : object required : - userId - messageId properties : userId : type : string messageId : type : string responses : "200" : description : Full message detail content : application/json : schema : $ref : "#/components/schemas/MessageDetailDTO" "400" : description : Invalid input "401" : description : Caller is not authorised "404" : description : Message not found or not owned by user "500" : description : Downstream failure /mark-message-read : post : summary : Mark a message as read and optionally return updated unread count description : > Marks the specified message as read for the given user, persists the change via MessageSystemAPI, and can optionally recalculate and return the new unread count. requestBody : required : true content : application/json : schema : type : object required : - userId - messageId properties : userId : type : string messageId : type : string returnUnreadCount : type : boolean description : "If true, return updated unreadCount" default : true responses : "200" : description : Message marked as read and unread count returned (if requested) content : application/json : schema : type : object properties : success : type : boolean example : true unreadCount : type : integer description : "Updated unread count after marking read" x-notes : > If the caller does not require unreadCount, they may ignore the response body and treat HTTP 200 as success only. "204" : description : Message marked as read with no response body "400" : description : Invalid request (e.g. missing userId/messageId) "401" : description : Caller is not authorised "404" : description : Message not found or not owned by user "500" : description : Downstream failure components : schemas : UnreadMessagesResult : type : object description : "Aggregated unread messages for a user, including system and bulk" properties : userId : type : string totalUnread : type : integer messages : type : array items : $ref : "#/components/schemas/MessageSummaryDTO" MessageSummaryDTO : type : object description : "Lightweight message representation used in inbox list" required : - messageId - title - type - status - timestampUtc properties : messageId : type : string title : type : string summary : type : string description : "Short preview of the message content" type : type : string description : "Message type: system or bulk" enum : [ system , bulk ] status : type : string description : "Read/unread status" enum : [ read , unread ] category : type : string description : "Optional category (e.g. Account, Dividend, CorporateAction)" timestampUtc : type : string format : date-time description : "Message creation time (UTC)" localizedTimestamp : type : string description : "Human-friendly timestamp formatted for user's locale (optional)" actions : type : array description : "Available actions (e.g. download, acknowledge)" items : type : string pushNotification : type : boolean description : "Whether this message should trigger a push notification" MessageDetailDTO : type : object description : "Full message details returned for a single message" required : - messageId - title - content - type - status - timestampUtc properties : messageId : type : string title : type : string content : type : string description : "Full message body as rendered to the user" type : type : string enum : [ system , bulk ] status : type : string enum : [ read , unread ] category : type : string timestampUtc : type : string format : date-time localizedTimestamp : type : string actions : type : array items : type : string pushNotification : type : boolean metadata : type : object additionalProperties : type : string description : "Optional metadata key-value pairs from upstream systems" security : - internalServiceAuth : [] components : securitySchemes : internalServiceAuth : type : http scheme : bearer bearerFormat : JWT description : "Internal service-to-service authentication token" Commentary for Developers ¶ Why POST for process endpoints? These are internal orchestration operations that may evolve over time and accept complex filter/payload objects. Using POST avoids overloading query strings and makes it easier to extend the request structure without breaking URLs. Relationship to Channel API: InvestorInboxChannelAPI exposes: GET /messages/unread GET /messages/{messageId} PATCH /messages/{messageId}/read Internally, it calls InvestorInboxProcessAPI using the contracts defined above: /unread-messages /message-detail /mark-message-read The Channel API mostly does HTTP concerns (auth, headers, rate limiting, mapping DTOs), while the Process API owns business logic & orchestration . Where integration happens: All calls to MessageSystemAPI , UserPreferenceSystemAPI , and BulkMessageSystemAPI are inside InvestorInboxProcessAPI , not exposed here. This ensures: Single place for validation, error handling and retries. Clear separation between domain logic and system-specific contracts. How to implement: Use this OpenAPI spec to generate stubs or controllers for InvestorInboxProcessAPI . Implement the orchestration logic described in the Sequence Diagrams and Functional Notes documents. Ensure that UnreadMessagesResult , MessageSummaryDTO , and MessageDetailDTO align with: Inbox list UI requirements. Detail view UI requirements. Push notification decisions. Together with the Assumptions , SPC Architecture Overview , and Sequence Diagrams , this file completes the Low-Level Design (LLD) specification for the InvestorInboxProcessAPI .

docs.text: Assumptions for Message Inbox API Design (LLD) ¶ Architecture Assumptions ¶ NOTE – This Low-Level Design (LLD) primarily defines the Process API for the Message Inbox solution. Channel API considerations are included to outline how the UI will consume the messages (pagination, caching, unread counts, push handling). System API considerations are treated as upstream dependencies assumed to already exist (raw data, bulk store, user preferences, message metadata). The focus of this LLD is on orchestration, validation, transformation, unread computation, and integration logic inside the Process API , because that is where the actual business rules, aggregation, and message preparation for the client occur. SPC Architecture ¶ The API design follows a System → Process → Channel (SPC) architecture. System APIs provide raw data. Process APIs orchestrate, validate, transform, and compute unread counts. Channel APIs expose endpoints to web and mobile clients. Pull-Based Model ¶ The solution is primarily pull-based; users fetch messages when they log in or refresh their inbox. System messages are user-specific and available immediately on login. Bulk messages exist in a centralized bulk message store; they are aggregated and filtered per user at fetch time. Push Notifications (Optional / Complementary) ¶ High-priority messages may trigger push notifications or in-app alerts. Push notifications only signal the user; full message content is retrieved via the pull API. Central Bulk Message System ¶ A centralized system manages the creation and storage of bulk messages for multiple users. Users do not store bulk messages locally until they fetch them from the Process API. Multi-Device Support ¶ Users may access the inbox via multiple devices (mobile and web). Read/unread status must be synchronized across devices. Offline Caching ¶ Mobile clients cache unread message IDs and content for offline viewing. Web clients may cache in session storage. Offline updates (e.g., marking a message read) are synced once online. Error Handling ¶ Partial failures in System APIs or Bulk APIs do not break the entire inbox fetch. Error codes include standard HTTP responses: 401 , 404 , 500 . Functional Assumptions ¶ Message Types ¶ System Messages: Critical updates, account changes, corporate actions. Bulk Messages: Aggregated notifications, such as dividends or portfolio updates. Validation & Transformation ¶ All messages must have mandatory fields: messageId , title , content , timestamp . Bulk messages are aggregated and filtered per user. Timestamps may be localized based on user preferences. Unread / Read Tracking ¶ Unread counts are maintained on the client and in the Process API. Read status updates propagate to all devices for consistency. Scalability ¶ Users may have hundreds or thousands of messages. Pagination and filtering are applied to reduce payloads. Security ¶ APIs are secured with JWT authentication. User ID is validated from the token for all API calls. Push Notifications ¶ Only messages flagged pushNotification: true trigger notifications. Notification respects user preferences (opt-in/out). Aggregation ¶ Bulk messages are aggregated per user at fetch time. Aggregation ensures that each user sees only relevant messages. Operational Assumptions ¶ System APIs and Bulk APIs are assumed to be available and responsive most of the time. Messages remain in the inbox until marked read or archived. Push notifications may be delayed in case of device offline or network issues. The design allows new message types or additional backend systems to be integrated without major changes.

docs.text: Developer Notes ¶ All DTO schemas are defined inside the OpenAPI under components.schemas . Treat those as the canonical data contracts for the Message Inbox LLD. Caching ¶ Mobile: Use local cache (e.g. SQLite / secure storage) for messages[] and totalUnread . Refresh cache on: app resume, explicit pull-to-refresh, successful mark-as-read. Web: Use session storage (or in-memory cache) for the current page of messages. Always re-fetch on full page reload or login. Rules: Cache is an optimization only – server state (Process/System APIs) is source of truth. After any mutating operation (mark read), either: update cache locally, and/or re-fetch /messages/unread to reconcile. Push Notifications ¶ Triggering: Process layer (or upstream command services) should only trigger push when: status = "unread" , pushNotification = true , user preferences allow notifications. Behaviour after read: Once message is marked read: no further notifications for that message, decremented badge count on device (if supported by push provider). Delivery: Use existing notification infrastructure (e.g. Firebase/APNs) via a NotificationDispatchService . Device token management and invalid token cleanup handled centrally, not in inbox code. Edge Cases ¶ Offline mode (mobile): Allow reading from cached messages. Queue mark-read requests locally and replay when online. After sync, re-fetch unread messages to reconcile unreadCount . Partial message fetch: If one downstream system fails (e.g. BulkMessageSystemAPI), still return what is available. Use flags such as partialResult and/or degradedMode to inform UI. Multi-device sync: Read state is persisted in MessageSystemAPI . Any device calling /messages/unread sees the same latest status and unreadCount . Duplicate prevention: Deduplicate by messageId when merging system + bulk sources. Testing Recommendations ¶ Functional: Validate unread count after each mark-message-read call. Verify that bulk + system messages are merged and sorted correctly. Test filters (by status , category , date range) and pagination boundaries. Negative & security: Requests with invalid/missing Authorization → 401 . Requests where userId in payload does not match JWT → 403 . Accessing a message not owned by user → 403 / 404 (as per design). Resilience: Simulate downstream failures: Bulk API down, User preferences API delayed. Confirm partialResult behaviour and logging. Offline & sync: Simulate offline mark-read queueing and later reconciliation. Ensure unread badges align after reconnect + refresh. Security ¶ Authentication & Authorization: Use JWT bearer tokens at Channel API level. Process API should receive an already-authenticated principal (service-to-service auth). Always validate that userId in payload matches the subject in the token (ownership). Data protection: Treat message content as potentially sensitive (account / corporate info). Avoid logging full content; log IDs and correlation IDs instead. Audit: Audit log for: message read events, bulk message creation, security violations (ownership failures). Performance ¶ Pagination: Enforce page size limits (default 20, max 50) to prevent huge payloads. Keep sorting stable ( timestampUtc desc) to avoid issues with paging. Aggregation & orchestration: Prefer a single call from Channel → Process for unread messages. Inside Process API: fan-out to System APIs in parallel where possible, aggregate results, dedupe, map DTOs. Assumptions ¶ Mobile/web apps: cache unread IDs / message summaries locally for performance, always reconcile with backend periodically. System APIs: expose stable identifiers and timestamps, are generally available and within agreed SLAs. Notification infrastructure: already exists (e.g. Firebase/APNs push layer), handles device token management and low-level delivery concerns. Bulk messages: are precomputed and stored in Bulk/Message systems, are filtered per user by the Process layer before returning to clients. Additional Developer Considerations ¶ DTO versioning: If MessageSummaryDTO / MessageDetailDTO evolve, add fields in a backward-compatible way. For breaking changes, consider versioned endpoints or versioned DTOs. Idempotency: mark-message-read must be idempotent: repeated calls for the same messageId must not double-decrement unreadCount . Observability: Implement structured logging with correlation IDs per request. Expose metrics: latency per endpoint, count of degraded responses, error-rate per downstream dependency. Configuration: Page sizes, notification thresholds, and retention windows should be configurable (not hard-coded). These Developer Notes, together with the OpenAPI spec , Functional Notes , Assumptions , and Sequence Diagrams , are intended to give engineers everything they need to implement and operate the Message Inbox APIs confidently.

docs.text: Functional Notes ¶ Message Types: system — generated by core transactional systems (address changed, account opened, statements ready). bulk — generated for events affecting multiple users (dividend applied, corporate events). Critical Fields: messageId , userId , type , status , timestampUtc category — domain grouping (e.g., Profile, Dividends, CorporateAction) actions — UI actions (view, download, acknowledge) pushNotification — controls notification dispatch Validation Rules: User must be authenticated userId in JWT must match user in payload (ownership check) messageId must belong to user title and content are mandatory type must be system or bulk timestampUtc must be valid ISO 8601 category must be valid domain enum If pushNotification = true , verify user notification preferences If message action is acknowledge , enforce that message cannot be auto-dismissed Read state transitions must be valid (cannot un-read) Transformations: Merge system messages + bulk messages Sort descending by timestampUtc Map backend entity to MessageSummaryDTO and MessageDetailDTO Localize timestamps using user locale/timezone Truncate content to form summary text Convert internal backend enums/flags into UI-friendly values Strip internal metadata not required by UI Remove duplicate messages where system + bulk overlap If backend message actions reference internal codes, normalize them to canonical UI actions Unread Count Handling: unreadCount is persisted in message store unreadCount is exposed via /messages/unread unreadCount decrements when marking message as read multi-device sync is mandatory — next login always reflects persisted read state local cache is permitted for UI performance but must refresh on app resume optimistic updates allowed but must reconcile on re-fetch Push Notifications: Triggered only when: message is unread and pushNotification = true and user preference allows notifications After message is marked read: stop further notifications , remove badge count on mobile device Device token lookup performed during notification dispatch Pagination & Filtering: page & pageSize supported to avoid large payloads Default page size: 20 Maximum allowed page size: 50 Optional filtering: by message type (bulk | system) by category (corporate action, account change, security updates) by unread status Paging must be stable: identical sort order guarantees correct cursor movement Error Handling: 401 Unauthorized — invalid JWT or missing internal auth 404 Message Not Found — invalid id or not owned by user 500 Internal Server Error — downstream bulk/system failures Partial failures: If one upstream API fails, still return messages from others and mark partialResult flag Developer must log root cause + request ID Edge Cases: Offline mobile: cached messages allowed & read operations queued and reconciled when online Partial fetch tolerance: If bulk API fails, return system messages only + flag degradedMode Duplicate prevention: Deduplicate by messageId Large inbox: enforce paging/windowing strategy and avoid full payload returns

docs.text: Message Types: system — generated by core transactional systems (address changed, account opened, statements ready). bulk — generated for events affecting multiple users (dividend applied, corporate events). Critical Fields: messageId , userId , type , status , timestampUtc category — domain grouping (e.g., Profile, Dividends, CorporateAction) actions — UI actions (view, download, acknowledge) pushNotification — controls notification dispatch Validation Rules: User must be authenticated userId in JWT must match user in payload (ownership check) messageId must belong to user title and content are mandatory type must be system or bulk timestampUtc must be valid ISO 8601 category must be valid domain enum If pushNotification = true , verify user notification preferences If message action is acknowledge , enforce that message cannot be auto-dismissed Read state transitions must be valid (cannot un-read) Transformations: Merge system messages + bulk messages Sort descending by timestampUtc Map backend entity to MessageSummaryDTO and MessageDetailDTO Localize timestamps using user locale/timezone Truncate content to form summary text Convert internal backend enums/flags into UI-friendly values Strip internal metadata not required by UI Remove duplicate messages where system + bulk overlap If backend message actions reference internal codes, normalize them to canonical UI actions Unread Count Handling: unreadCount is persisted in message store unreadCount is exposed via /messages/unread unreadCount decrements when marking message as read multi-device sync is mandatory — next login always reflects persisted read state local cache is permitted for UI performance but must refresh on app resume optimistic updates allowed but must reconcile on re-fetch Push Notifications: Triggered only when: message is unread and pushNotification = true and user preference allows notifications After message is marked read: stop further notifications , remove badge count on mobile device Device token lookup performed during notification dispatch Pagination & Filtering: page & pageSize supported to avoid large payloads Default page size: 20 Maximum allowed page size: 50 Optional filtering: by message type (bulk | system) by category (corporate action, account change, security updates) by unread status Paging must be stable: identical sort order guarantees correct cursor movement Error Handling: 401 Unauthorized — invalid JWT or missing internal auth 404 Message Not Found — invalid id or not owned by user 500 Internal Server Error — downstream bulk/system failures Partial failures: If one upstream API fails, still return messages from others and mark partialResult flag Developer must log root cause + request ID Edge Cases: Offline mobile: cached messages allowed & read operations queued and reconciled when online Partial fetch tolerance: If bulk API fails, return system messages only + flag degradedMode Duplicate prevention: Deduplicate by messageId Large inbox: enforce paging/windowing strategy and avoid full payload returns

docs.text: API Request + Response Examples ¶ 1️⃣ API: GET /messages/unread ¶ Purpose: Fetch unread messages for inbox list (system + bulk). Example Request ¶ GET /messages/unread?page=1&pageSize=20 Authorization: Bearer <JWT> Example Response ¶ { "page" : 1 , "pageSize" : 20 , "totalUnread" : 4 , "messages" : [ { "messageId" : "12345" , "title" : "Address Change Confirmation" , "summary" : "Your address has been updated successfully" , "type" : "system" , "status" : "unread" , "timestampUtc" : "2025-12-04T09:15:00Z" , "category" : "Account" , "actions" : [ "acknowledge" ], "pushNotification" : true }, { "messageId" : "67890" , "title" : "Dividend Applied" , "summary" : "December dividends applied to your portfolio" , "type" : "bulk" , "status" : "unread" , "timestampUtc" : "2025-12-04T08:00:00Z" , "category" : "Finance" , "actions" : [ "download" ], "pushNotification" : false } ], "hasMore" : true } Notes ¶ UI loads pages incrementally Unread count reflects persisted state Local cache allowed, but must refresh on resume 2️⃣ API: GET /messages/unread (Degraded Mode) ¶ Purpose: Bulk API failed — inbox still loads using system messages. Example Response ¶ { "totalUnread" : 2 , "partialResult" : true , "messages" : [ { "messageId" : "88888" , "title" : "Statement Ready" , "summary" : "Your statement is available for download" , "type" : "system" , "status" : "unread" , "timestampUtc" : "2025-12-03T12:10:00Z" , "category" : "Finance" , "actions" : [ "download" ], "pushNotification" : false } ] } Notes ¶ partialResult=true signals degraded mode UI should still operate normally Logging mandatory for root-cause traceability 3️⃣ API: POST /message-detail ¶ Purpose: Retrieve full message content for detail view. Example Request ¶ { "userId" : "U100001" , "messageId" : "12345" } Example Response ¶ { "messageId" : "12345" , "title" : "Address Change Confirmation" , "content" : "Your address has been successfully updated and no additional actions are required." , "type" : "system" , "status" : "unread" , "timestampUtc" : "2025-12-04T09:15:00Z" , "localizedTimestamp" : "04 Dec 2025, 09:15 AM" , "category" : "Account" , "actions" : [ "acknowledge" ], "pushNotification" : true , "metadata" : { "changeType" : "profileUpdate" , "requiresAcknowledgement" : true } } Notes ¶ Ownership validation enforced Content may include legal wording or formatted text UI should optionally show metadata-driven actions 4️⃣ API: POST /mark-message-read ¶ Purpose: Persist read state + reduce unread count. Example Request ¶ { "userId" : "U100001" , "messageId" : "12345" , "returnUnreadCount" : true } Example Response ¶ { "success" : true , "unreadCount" : 3 } Notes ¶ Must update UI immediately (optimistic update) Reconcile after next fetch Prevent invalid transition (cannot "unread") 5️⃣ API: POST /mark-message-read (Already Read) ¶ Purpose: Demonstrates valid read state constraints. Example Response ¶ { "success" : false , "reason" : "MessageAlreadyRead" , "unreadCount" : 3 } 6️⃣ API: POST /message-detail (Security Violation) ¶ Purpose: Ownership enforcement Example Response ¶ { "error" : "MessageNotOwned" , "statusCode" : 403 , "message" : "The requested message does not belong to the authenticated user" } 7️⃣ API: GET /messages/unread With Filters ¶ Purpose: Narrow inbox by category or status Request ¶ GET /messages/unread?status=unread&category=CorporateAction&page=1&pageSize=20 Authorization: Bearer <JWT> Response ¶ { "page" : 1 , "pageSize" : 20 , "filters" : { "status" : "unread" , "category" : "CorporateAction" }, "totalUnread" : 6 , "messages" : [ { "messageId" : "99123" , "title" : "Corporate Restructuring Notice" , "summary" : "Corporate restructuring that affects your portfolio" , "type" : "bulk" , "status" : "unread" , "timestampUtc" : "2025-11-30T11:00:00Z" , "category" : "CorporateAction" , "actions" : [ "view" ], "pushNotification" : true } ], "hasMore" : true } 8️⃣ API: POST /mark-message-read — Offline Queue ¶ Purpose: Offline-safe mutation Response ¶ { "success" : true , "syncState" : "queued" , "localCacheUpdated" : true , "messageId" : "99123" } Notes ¶ Local UI marks read immediately Sync occurs on reconnect Must reconcile unreadCount on next fetch 9️⃣ API: GET /messages/unread — After Reconciliation ¶ { "totalUnread" : 5 , "messages" : [ { "messageId" : "44555" , "title" : "Profile Updated" , "summary" : "Your personal profile is fully verified" , "type" : "system" , "status" : "unread" , "timestampUtc" : "2025-12-01T10:20:00Z" , "category" : "Profile" , "actions" : [ "acknowledge" ], "pushNotification" : false } ] }

docs.text: Message Inbox API: Problem Statement, Objective, and Overview ¶ Problem Statement ¶ Investors and stakeholders need a centralized, reliable, and real-time message inbox to receive updates related to their accounts and investments. Messages can include: System-level messages: Critical updates like account changes, corporate actions, or address updates. Bulk messages: Updates such as dividend notifications, corporate action summaries, or other aggregated portfolio information. Key challenges include: Integration Complexity: Messages originate from multiple backend systems, such as account management, corporate actions, and dividend processing systems. Multi-channel Access: Users access messages via mobile and web applications. Real-time Notifications: High-priority messages require push notifications or in-app alerts. Unread/Read Tracking: Messages must maintain consistent read/unread status across all devices. Scalability: Users may have hundreds or thousands of messages, requiring aggregation and pagination. Validation & Transformation: Messages from different sources may vary in structure and require standardization before display. Objective ¶ Design a developer-ready Message Inbox API that: Aggregates messages from multiple backend sources. Validates and transforms messages for consistency. Supports multi-channel access (web and mobile) with caching for offline use. Tracks read/unread status accurately across devices. Triggers notifications for high-priority messages. Provides a complete OpenAPI specification ready for implementation. Overview of the Solution ¶ The solution uses a System → Process → Channel (SPC) API architecture : System APIs: Provide raw messages and user preferences. Process API: Orchestrates multiple System APIs. Applies validation and transformations. Computes unread counts. Triggers push notifications when required. Channel API: Exposes endpoints to web and mobile clients, manages caching, and delivers the final message data. Key Features: - Supports system and bulk messages. - Critical fields: messageId , title , content , timestamp , category , actions , pushNotification . - Pagination and filtering for large inboxes. - Local caching on mobile/web clients for offline access. - Error handling to manage partial system failures. This documentation provides OpenAPI specifications, mock responses, functional and developer notes , and diagrams showing architecture and user flows, intended for developer implementation.

docs.text: Sequence Diagrams – Message Inbox Low-Level Design (LLD) ¶ This section describes the runtime behaviour of the Message Inbox solution using sequence diagrams. It uses concrete component names so developers can map them directly to services and APIs. Components referenced: Investor Client (Web/Mobile) – the authenticated user interface (browser or mobile app). InvestorInboxChannelAPI – the channel-facing API layer exposing REST endpoints to clients. InvestorInboxProcessAPI – the process layer responsible for orchestration, validation, transformation, and unread count computation. MessageSystemAPI – system API that exposes raw message data (system + persisted bulk messages). UserPreferenceSystemAPI – system API for user notification preferences and localisation settings. BulkMessageSystemAPI – system API that stores and serves bulk messages addressed to many users. (Optional) PushNotificationService – external service used by the platform to send push notifications to devices. 1️⃣ Sequence: Fetch Unread Messages on Login ¶ Goal: When the user logs in or opens the inbox, the client retrieves all unread messages (system + bulk), plus the totalUnread count. Flow (Step-by-Step): Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Sends a request to fetch unread messages: GET /messages/unread?userId={userId} to InvestorInboxChannelAPI . InvestorInboxChannelAPI Forwards the request to InvestorInboxProcessAPI using an internal call such as: FetchUnreadMessages(userId) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Calls: GetUserMessages(userId) to retrieve all user-specific system messages (e.g. address changes, corporate actions). InvestorInboxProcessAPI → UserPreferenceSystemAPI Calls: GetUserPreferences(userId) to retrieve user preferences (e.g. notification settings, locale, time zone). InvestorInboxProcessAPI → BulkMessageSystemAPI Calls: GetBulkMessagesForUser(userId) to get bulk messages relevant to this user (e.g. dividend events, portfolio-wide updates). System APIs → InvestorInboxProcessAPI MessageSystemAPI returns raw system messages. UserPreferenceSystemAPI returns user preferences. BulkMessageSystemAPI returns raw bulk messages filtered for this user. InvestorInboxProcessAPI (internal processing) Validates all messages (required fields, ownership, timestamp formats). Aggregates system and bulk messages into a unified list. Applies transformations: Localises timestamps using user preferences. Maps backend fields to the MessageSummary DTO. Computes totalUnread by counting messages with status = unread . Optionally determines which messages should set pushNotification = true . InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Returns a DTO such as: UnreadMessagesDTO { totalUnread, messages[] } InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Client Responds with: 200 OK + JSON ( totalUnread , messages[] ) Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Caches the messageId s and summary data locally (for fast rendering and offline support). Displays the unread badge/count and message list in the inbox UI. 2️⃣ Sequence: View Full Message Content ¶ Goal: When the user taps/clicks a message in the inbox, the client retrieves the full message content. Flow (Step-by-Step): Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Sends: GET /messages/{messageId} to InvestorInboxChannelAPI . InvestorInboxChannelAPI Calls InvestorInboxProcessAPI : GetMessageDetail(messageId, userId) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Calls: GetMessageById(messageId) to retrieve the raw message record. MessageSystemAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Returns the message entity, including ownership and all raw fields. InvestorInboxProcessAPI (internal processing) Validates that the messageId belongs to the current userId . Applies transformation/mapping: Raw entity → MessageDetailDTO (title, full content, type, category, actions, pushNotification flag, timestamp). Enforces any business rules (e.g. hide certain fields based on user role/preferences if needed). InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Returns: MessageDetailDTO InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Client Responds with: 200 OK + JSON (full message content) Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Renders full message content screen. May optimistically update local state to treat this message as “viewed”. 3️⃣ Sequence: Mark Message as Read & Sync Count ¶ Goal: When the user has read a message, the client marks it as read so that unread counts stay consistent across devices. Flow (Step-by-Step): Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Sends: PATCH /messages/{messageId}/read to InvestorInboxChannelAPI . InvestorInboxChannelAPI Calls InvestorInboxProcessAPI : MarkMessageRead(messageId, userId) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Calls: UpdateMessageReadFlag(messageId, userId) to persist the read status in the underlying message store. MessageSystemAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Returns a success result (e.g. Update OK ). InvestorInboxProcessAPI (internal processing) Optionally recalculates unreadCount for this user (or uses a cached counter that decrements by 1). Ensures that the change will be reflected in future calls to /messages/unread . InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Returns: Either no body ( 204 No Content ), or a small DTO with the new unreadCount . InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Client Responds with: 204 No Content or 200 OK + JSON with updated unread count. Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Updates the local cache to mark this message as read . Updates the badge/unread count in the UI. On next login (or on another device), the updated status will be fetched from the backend and stay consistent. 4️⃣ Sequence: Bulk Message Creation and Later Display ¶ Goal: Model how a bulk message (e.g. dividend notification) is created for many users and later appears in each user’s inbox. 4.1 Bulk Message Creation (Back-Office) ¶ Back-Office User (Dividend Ops Portal) Uses an internal portal to create a bulk message for a corporate event: e.g. “Dividend applied for Event X to eligible holders”. Dividend Ops Portal → BulkMessageSystemAPI Sends something like: CreateBulkMessage(dividendEventId, criteria) where criteria identifies which investors/users should receive it. BulkMessageSystemAPI → MessageSystemAPI Derives the list of affected userId s. Persists bulk message records linked to those users (or stores a reference + targeting rules). MessageSystemAPI → BulkMessageSystemAPI Confirms persistence of bulk message entries: Stored OK . At this stage, messages are available in backend storage , but users haven’t pulled them yet. 4.2 Bulk Message Delivery to Individual User ¶ Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Later, when an investor logs in or opens their inbox, it calls: GET /messages/unread?userId={userId} to InvestorInboxChannelAPI . InvestorInboxChannelAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Calls: FetchUnreadMessages(userId) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → BulkMessageSystemAPI Calls: GetBulkMessagesForUser(userId) to get just the bulk messages relevant to this user. InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Calls: GetUserMessages(userId) to fetch user-specific system messages. BulkMessageSystemAPI & MessageSystemAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Return: User-specific bulk messages. and User-specific system messages. InvestorInboxProcessAPI (internal processing) Merges and de-duplicates system and bulk messages. Validates, transforms, and maps to MessageSummary DTOs. Computes totalUnread . Applies any channel-specific or business rules (e.g., sort by timestamp descending). InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Returns: UnreadMessagesDTO containing totalUnread and messages[] . InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Client Returns: 200 OK + JSON. Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Renders bulk and system messages together in the inbox. Indicates unread status and, if applicable, any actions like “download statement”. 5️⃣ Sequence: Push Notification Dispatch → User Inbox Fetch ¶ Goal: When a bulk message or system message is created by back-office systems, push notifications are dispatched to affected investors. Once a user taps the notification on their device, the app pulls fresh unread messages from the inbox via the Channel API. Flow (Step-by-Step): BulkMessageCommandService OR SystemMessageCommandService Triggers a notification dispatch: notify(messageTemplate, eventType, targetCriteria) (e.g., dividend applied to eligible holders) NotificationDispatchService (internal) Determines affected investors based on targetCriteria Resolves device tokens for all impacted users Prepares a short notification payload using messageTemplate NotificationDispatchService → PushDeliveryProvider Sends: GetBulkMessagesForUser(userId) to a provider such as Firebase, APNS, or Azure Notification Hubs InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Delivers push notification to each registered device Device OS displays the notification to the user Investor Device (Mobile App) When the user taps the push notification: App opens message inbox UI Investor Device → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Sends: 'GET /messages/unread?userId={userId}` to fetch fresh unread messages, ensuring the latest persisted bulk/system messages are visible InvestorInboxChannelAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Internally executes FetchUnreadMessages(userId) (integration + transformation logic described in Sequence 1) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Device Responds with the refreshed inbox state: 200 OK + JSON (totalUnread, messages[]) Investor Device (Mobile App) Displays messages with correct unread badges User is now aligned with the backend state How Developers Should Use These Diagrams ¶ Treat InvestorInboxChannelAPI , InvestorInboxProcessAPI , MessageSystemAPI , UserPreferenceSystemAPI , and BulkMessageSystemAPI as concrete services or bounded contexts. Use the sequence diagrams to: Implement method signatures, DTOs, and orchestration logic. Ensure that read/unread status, bulk message handling, and push notification decisions are implemented in the InvestorInboxProcessAPI . Use the MessageSummary and MessageDetail models from the API spec to shape responses in the Channel API layer. These diagrams, together with the OpenAPI specification, Functional Notes, Assumptions, and Developer Notes , form a complete Low-Level Design (LLD) for the Message Inbox feature.

Applies transformation/mapping: Raw entity → MessageDetailDTO (title, full content, type, category, actions, pushNotification flag, timestamp). Enforces any business rules (e.g. hide certain fields based on user role/preferences if needed). InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Returns: MessageDetailDTO InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Client Responds with: 200 OK + JSON (full message content) Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Renders full message content screen. May optimistically update local state to treat this message as “viewed”.
docs.title: 2️⃣ Sequence: View Full Message Content

docs.text: Goal: When the user has read a message, the client marks it as read so that unread counts stay consistent across devices. Flow (Step-by-Step): Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Sends: PATCH /messages/{messageId}/read to InvestorInboxChannelAPI . InvestorInboxChannelAPI Calls InvestorInboxProcessAPI : MarkMessageRead(messageId, userId) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Calls: UpdateMessageReadFlag(messageId, userId) to persist the read status in the underlying message store. MessageSystemAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Returns a success result (e.g. Update OK ). InvestorInboxProcessAPI (internal processing) Optionally recalculates unreadCount for this user (or uses a cached counter that decrements by 1). Ensures that the change will be reflected in future calls to /messages/unread . InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Returns: Either no body ( 204 No Content ), or a small DTO with the new unreadCount . InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Client Responds with: 204 No Content or 200 OK + JSON with updated unread count. Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Updates the local cache to mark this message as read . Updates the badge/unread count in the UI. On next login (or on another device), the updated status will be fetched from the backend and stay consistent.
docs.title: 3️⃣ Sequence: Mark Message as Read & Sync Count

docs.text: Goal: Model how a bulk message (e.g. dividend notification) is created for many users and later appears in each user’s inbox.
docs.title: 4️⃣ Sequence: Bulk Message Creation and Later Display

docs.text: Back-Office User (Dividend Ops Portal) Uses an internal portal to create a bulk message for a corporate event: e.g. “Dividend applied for Event X to eligible holders”. Dividend Ops Portal → BulkMessageSystemAPI Sends something like: CreateBulkMessage(dividendEventId, criteria) where criteria identifies which investors/users should receive it. BulkMessageSystemAPI → MessageSystemAPI Derives the list of affected userId s. Persists bulk message records linked to those users (or stores a reference + targeting rules). MessageSystemAPI → BulkMessageSystemAPI Confirms persistence of bulk message entries: Stored OK . At this stage, messages are available in backend storage , but users haven’t pulled them yet.
docs.title: 4.1 Bulk Message Creation (Back-Office)

docs.text: Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Later, when an investor logs in or opens their inbox, it calls: GET /messages/unread?userId={userId} to InvestorInboxChannelAPI . InvestorInboxChannelAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Calls: FetchUnreadMessages(userId) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → BulkMessageSystemAPI Calls: GetBulkMessagesForUser(userId) to get just the bulk messages relevant to this user. InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Calls: GetUserMessages(userId) to fetch user-specific system messages. BulkMessageSystemAPI & MessageSystemAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Return: User-specific bulk messages. and User-specific system messages. InvestorInboxProcessAPI (internal processing) Merges and de-duplicates system and bulk messages. Validates, transforms, and maps to MessageSummary DTOs. Computes totalUnread . Applies any channel-specific or business rules (e.g., sort by timestamp descending). InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Returns: UnreadMessagesDTO containing totalUnread and messages[] . InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Client Returns: 200 OK + JSON. Investor Client (Web/Mobile) Renders bulk and system messages together in the inbox. Indicates unread status and, if applicable, any actions like “download statement”.
docs.title: 4.2 Bulk Message Delivery to Individual User

docs.text: Goal: When a bulk message or system message is created by back-office systems, push notifications are dispatched to affected investors. Once a user taps the notification on their device, the app pulls fresh unread messages from the inbox via the Channel API. Flow (Step-by-Step): BulkMessageCommandService OR SystemMessageCommandService Triggers a notification dispatch: notify(messageTemplate, eventType, targetCriteria) (e.g., dividend applied to eligible holders) NotificationDispatchService (internal) Determines affected investors based on targetCriteria Resolves device tokens for all impacted users Prepares a short notification payload using messageTemplate NotificationDispatchService → PushDeliveryProvider Sends: GetBulkMessagesForUser(userId) to a provider such as Firebase, APNS, or Azure Notification Hubs InvestorInboxProcessAPI → MessageSystemAPI Delivers push notification to each registered device Device OS displays the notification to the user Investor Device (Mobile App) When the user taps the push notification: App opens message inbox UI Investor Device → InvestorInboxChannelAPI Sends: 'GET /messages/unread?userId={userId}` to fetch fresh unread messages, ensuring the latest persisted bulk/system messages are visible InvestorInboxChannelAPI → InvestorInboxProcessAPI Internally executes FetchUnreadMessages(userId) (integration + transformation logic described in Sequence 1) InvestorInboxProcessAPI → InvestorInboxChannelAPI → Investor Device Responds with the refreshed inbox state: 200 OK + JSON (totalUnread, messages[]) Investor Device (Mobile App) Displays messages with correct unread badges User is now aligned with the backend state
docs.title: 5️⃣ Sequence: Push Notification Dispatch → User Inbox Fetch

docs.text: Treat InvestorInboxChannelAPI , InvestorInboxProcessAPI , MessageSystemAPI , UserPreferenceSystemAPI , and BulkMessageSystemAPI as concrete services or bounded contexts. Use the sequence diagrams to: Implement method signatures, DTOs, and orchestration logic. Ensure that read/unread status, bulk message handling, and push notification decisions are implemented in the InvestorInboxProcessAPI . Use the MessageSummary and MessageDetail models from the API spec to shape responses in the Channel API layer. These diagrams, together with the OpenAPI specification, Functional Notes, Assumptions, and Developer Notes , form a complete Low-Level Design (LLD) for the Message Inbox feature.
docs.title: How Developers Should Use These Diagrams

docs.text: SPC Architecture Overview ¶ The SPC (System – Process – Channel) architecture is a layered API design pattern used to logically separate responsibilities. It helps simplify solution design, maximize reuse, and improve scalability and maintainability. System APIs ¶ Primary Role: Provide raw, unprocessed data directly from backend systems. System APIs: - Interact with source systems or databases - Expose reusable CRUD-style endpoints - Contain minimal or no business rules - Perform basic input/output validation only - Maintain a stable interface across consumers Example System APIs - GetUserProfile - GetAccountData - GetHoldings - GetRawMessages Process APIs ¶ Primary Role: Orchestrate business rules and convert raw data into client-ready output. Process APIs: - Call and combine multiple System APIs - Apply transformations, enrichment, filtering, aggregation - Validate fields, enforce security and authorization - Implement message formatting, unread count logic, caching, and data normalization - Contain all business logic for inbox processing Example Process APIs - GetUserInbox - ComputeUnreadCount - PrepareDividendMessageFeed Channel APIs ¶ Primary Role: Deliver the final API output to client-facing applications (mobile, web, portals). Channel APIs: - Adapt Process API outputs for specific channels - Apply pagination, sorting, localization, and UI formatting - Optimize responses for device performance and usability - Contain minimal logic; they depend on the Process API for actual computation Example Channel Endpoints - /messages/unread - /messages/latest - /messages/read/{id} How the Layers Work Together ¶ A user opens the web application or mobile app. The Channel API receives a request (e.g., /messages/unread ). The Channel API forwards the request to an appropriate Process API . The Process API orchestrates backend calls: Queries multiple System APIs , such as SystemAPI_Messages and SystemAPI_UserPreferences Aggregates, filters, and validates returned data Applies message-level business rules (e.g., unread counts, formatting, priority logic) The Process API returns a complete, fully prepared payload to the Channel API. The Channel API formats this payload for the requesting device and returns the response. Business Value of SPC Architecture ¶ Why SPC matters Reusability System APIs serve multiple Process APIs without duplication. Clear Separation of Concerns All orchestration and domain rules reside in Process APIs — Channel APIs remain lightweight. Scalability Channel APIs scale independently and enable channel-specific optimization (mobile, web, portals). Maintainability Feature enhancements and new use cases only require changes at the Process layer, preserving Channel and System stability. Typical Use Cases ¶ Where SPC shines in a Message Inbox solution: Building actionable unread messages from multiple backend sources Enforcing read/unread tracking and cross-device synchronization Merging bulk and system messages into a unified inbox Localizing timestamps, applying preferences, and formatting content Delivering client-ready outputs optimized for UX and performance End of SPC Architecture Overview
